raw: 42.1 Red Cell Analysis and Adversarial Wargaming
teaching_note: A red cell tests an assessment from an explicitly assigned alternative perspective; a tabletop game explores conditional decisions and consequences under rules. Neither produces evidence of an actual adversary's intentions or a forecast simply because a narrative is coherent. In a paper-only fictional archive exercise, challenge the favored explanation of a delayed catalogue with routine review, transcription error, and missing records; stop before deriving live exploitation, persuasion, or action plans. Inherited AI-security citations are context, not evidence that a red-cell method is accurate [@official_cia_tradecraft_primer].
title: Red Cell Analysis and Adversarial Wargaming

raw: 42.2 Network Analysis: Link Charts, Activity Matrices, Social Network Analysis
teaching_note: **Synthetic network record.** Nodes are documents A (archive release), B (newsletter), and C (digest); edges A→B and B→C mean 'copied text from', supported by supplied version cards, not communication, control, or intent. A document-by-claim matrix shows all three repeat the same date, yielding one origin rather than three confirmations. Centrality in this tiny, selected graph says nothing about credibility or causal importance; changing an edge definition changes its meaning. Missing edges may reflect missing observation, and STIX/TAXII specify exchange formats rather than validating social-network conclusions; no real people or accounts are mapped [@ageint266].
title: Network Analysis: Link Charts, Activity Matrices, Social Network Analysis

teaching_note: **Completed synthetic chronology.** Card A reports at 09:00 that a fictional catalogue was approved at 08:30; B is a 09:10 copy; C reports at 10:00 that approval is still pending but has no event timestamp. Separate event time, report time, timezone, source version, and unknown intervals: C cannot be placed after the approval as an event merely because it was reported later. The initial conclusion is an unresolved status conflict, not that approval was reversed or deliberately concealed. A supplied correction C2 says C described 08:00, removing the conflict and yielding 'pending at 08:00, approved at 08:30'; causal reasons remain unknown. Temporal order alone cannot establish why approval occurred [@official_odni_icd_203; @ageint266].
title: Timeline Analysis and Event Sequencing

teaching_note: Translate 'Will the fictional catalogue appear by noon?' into the discriminating gap 'Is there an authorized publication record before 12:00?', with a supplied registry card as the allowed source and a stated review time. No notice is weak negative evidence if the registry was offline or never recorded draft releases; absence matters only with an expected reporting process and opportunity to observe. Use instructor-provided cards, not real tasking or contact, and abstain if resolution coverage is missing. Transport standards and security catalogues do not supply a theory of collection adequacy [@official_odni_icd_206].
title: Collection Management: Requirements, Gaps, and Observation Opportunity

raw: 42.5 Writing Intelligence Products: Assessments, Estimates, Warnings
teaching_note: An assessment interprets present/past evidence; an estimate addresses future or otherwise uncertain conditions; a warning highlights a consequential possibility, indicators, and decision timing without pretending certainty. A completed fictional assessment reads: 'Approval at 08:30 is supported after C2 corrected the event time; publication by noon remains uncertain; newsletter and digest are dependent copies, and no inference about intent follows.' A warning could identify a missed scheduled publication slot, but must include its expected observation opportunity and benign alternatives. The product's polish is not its evidence [@official_odni_icd_203; @official_odni_icd_206].
title: Writing Intelligence Products: Assessments, Estimates, Warnings

raw: 42.6 Communicating Uncertainty: Analytic Line vs. Raw Reporting
teaching_note: **Completed synthetic forecast.** At 09:00 register 'catalogue published before 12:00 today', resolve only from the supplied authorized publication registry, and assign p=0.60 with low analytic confidence because scheduling evidence is incomplete. At 10:00 a supplied delay card changes p to 0.30 without erasing the first forecast; the 11:30 registry card resolves y=1, giving the final forecast a Brier score (0.30−1)²=0.49. For a separate invented batch p=(0.75,0.75,0.25,0.25), y=(1,0,1,0), mean Brier=0.3125 versus 0.25 for constant 0.50; both probability bins resolve at 0.50, illustrating miscalibration in this tiny batch, not estimating enduring skill. Proper scores reflect calibration and other aspects of forecast quality; one outcome cannot establish calibration. Likelihood concerns the event, confidence concerns the evidential basis: 'likely, low confidence' and 'unlikely, high confidence' are coherent combinations; none is a causal effect estimate [@official_odni_icd_203].
title: Communicating Uncertainty: Forecasts, Confidence, and Calibration

raw: 42.7 Machine-Assisted Analysis: When to Automate, When to Require Human Judgment
teaching_note: Automate bounded extraction or duplicate grouping only with traceable source spans; retain human responsibility for framing, ambiguous timestamps, alternative explanations, and release decisions. In a supplied fictional grading record, reviewer R1 awards 2/3 for independence handling and R2 awards 3/3 because the model calls A/B/C corroboration; adjudication restores 2/3 after the copy edges are inspected. Those invented ratings illustrate disagreement resolution, not measured inter-rater reliability or model capability. If the source locator, registry coverage, or contradiction cannot be checked, hold the claim rather than accepting fluent machine text as new evidence [@official_odni_icd_203; @official_odni_icd_206; @sec:analytic-workflow].
title: Machine-Assisted Analysis: Automation, Independent Review, and Abstention
